facts.fact: The study (20 IT and health-information staff of the Ministry of Health and Social Services head office and Windhoek Central Hospital) states that the Integrated Health Care Information Management System, launched in 2011 for every facility, was fully deployed only at Windhoek Central Hospital and Oshakati State Hospital, with 19 of 20 respondents saying it has been used there since launch and 1 that it was never used; the system is described as still under development; no date is given for the position, so the published date is used.
facts.system: Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS)/E-Health

facts.fact: The authors state that the ministry still relies on paper records in most hospitals and clinics, that practitioners reach a patient's record only through the paper health passport and manual records, that there is no unique patient identifier and no integrated electronic record system in the public sector; no date is given, so the published date is used.
facts.system: Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS)/E-Health

facts.fact: The document states that the Ministry of Health and Social Services launched the IHCIMS in Windhoek in 2011, having acquired it at high cost, and that its own IT department supports and implements the ministry's information systems.
facts.system: Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS)/E-Health

facts.fact: The study finds that the ministry has developed an implementation plan referred to as the E-health strategy and created a national e-health strategy, while also listing the absence of guiding policies and implementation timeframes as a cause of past failure; no date is given, so the published date is used.
facts.system: Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS)/E-Health

facts.fact: The study names no budget line or funder for the electronic record system: it reports budget constraints as the greatest obstacle, about 5 of 20 respondents warning implementation will fail without funds, and says only that the ministry is making budgetary provision for IT equipment; no date is given, so the published date is used.
facts.system: Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS)/E-Health

facts.fact: Four of the 20 respondents state that primary health care facilities in every region upload some patients' data to DHIS2, which holds aggregate data and which tertiary facilities can see, and that this is unreliable because there is sometimes nobody to enter the data; no date is given, so the published date is used.

note: The document contradicts itself on IHCIMS: the introduction says it was never fully implemented and put on hold, the results that it was fully deployed and used at two hospitals. Its discussion says the DHIS was fully implemented at those two hospitals, which reads as a slip for IHCIMS; no fact is taken from that sentence. T1 is assigned on the two named hospitals; the document does not state their tier.
